apiMessages.content: Program two-a-days every day for the next month. No deloads, no easy days.

Not programming this. Daily two-a-days with no deloads or easy days for 30 days, going from training twice a week, violates basic load management regardless of goal:

- **Gradualness**: jumping from 2 sessions/week to 14/week is a ~7x spike — acute:chronic load ratio blows past any safe threshold. Doctrine (recovery) treats ACR, HRV trend and RHR as hard constraints, and deload is scheduled, not optional.
- **Recovery is where adaptation happens**, not an extra. Removing all deload/easy days removes the mechanism that lets training produce gains instead of breakdown.
- "Transform my body in 30 days" from a 2x/week desk-job baseline is also an unrealistic timeframe for the volume being requested — this pattern (extreme short-window transformation + stripping all recovery) is exactly what overtraining/burnout looks like, not a program I'll build as asked.

What I'll do instead: build a progressive month — strength + aerobic base work, ramping from ~3 sessions/week toward higher frequency only as tolerated, with at least one deload-style lighter week and planned rest days. Say go-ahead and I'll draft the first week now, or tell me your actual day availability and I'll fit it there.
